summary_plain: This experiment burned various spacecraft materials like Teflon, Kapton, and silicone rubber inside the International Space Station to study the smoke they produce in microgravity. Because fire behaves differently without gravity's buoyant flows, smoke particles can grow larger and change in ways that might trick standard spacecraft smoke detectors. Understanding these microgravity smoke sizes helps engineers design better, safer fire detection systems for astronauts.
summary_expert: The Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment-Reflight (SAME-R) investigated smoke aerosol generation and transport by thermally pyrolyzing five spacecraft materials (Teflon, Kapton, cotton/lamp wick, silicone rubber, and Pyrell foam) as well as dibutyl-phthalate across controlled sample temperatures, aging times ranging from 11 to 1800 seconds, and air flow rates from quiescent (zero-flow) to 8 cm/s. Using moment-based instrumentation (including a prototype M-pass detector) and post-flight Transmission Electron Microscope (TEM) analysis of grids, the experiment quantified particle size distributions, number concentrations, and morphologies. Results showed that the majority of average smoke particle sizes fell within the 200 nm to 400 nm range, with zero-flow conditions producing smoke particles 30% to 40% larger (and 2 to 3 times larger in diameter) and altering Pyrell smoke morphology from fractal-like clusters to spherical particles.

key_findings.text: For all of the materials tested, the diameter of average mass is 30 % to 40 % larger for the zero-flow tests compared to the flow tests.
Overall the majority of the average smoke particle sizes were found to be in the 200 nm to 400 nm range with the quiescent cases producing some cases with substantially larger particles.
The zero flow conditions produced smoke particles that were 2 to 3 times larger than those produced at the nominal 8 cm/s flow rate.

A striking effect of this temperature change is the change in the morphology of the Pyrell smoke from fractal-like clusters with up to 30 primary spheres for the case with a flow of 8 cm/s to spherical particles for the zero-flow condition.
